## One vector, several notations {#iv1-notation .vector-lesson}

<div data-vector="notation" class="v-static"></div>

$$\mathbf a \qquad \underset{\sim}{a} \qquad \overrightarrow{AB}$$

The arrow runs from **tail $A$** to **head $B$**. Its length represents magnitude.

$$\lvert\mathbf a\rvert\qquad\lvert\underset{\sim}{a}\rvert\qquad\lvert\overrightarrow{AB}\rvert$$

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §1.2 · p. 1 · The same notation applies in 2D and 3D.</div>

::: notes
Bold is convenient in printed slides; the undertilde matches the booklet and handwritten work. All three vector notations shown can denote the same vector. Magnitude is a non-negative scalar. Distinguish the directed vector AB from a bare segment or the distance AB. No component notation is required here.
:::
